title: The postcard
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: A postcard from Seattle in tiny manic handwriting. Wood reads it aloud to the dog. He edits.

panels.composition: Wood's bedroom. A postcard on the table: a photo of a needle-shaped tower. WOOD holding it. BARNABY under the table, listening because he's there.

characters.pose: under the table, one ear up

balloons.text: Listen to this. 'Wood — there is a gallery here that only shows things made of light.'

image.prompt: a young man at a bedroom drawing table reading a postcard of a needle-shaped tower aloud, a scruffy dog under the table with one ear up, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: The postcard's back: handwriting so small and dense it's a texture. Wood's thumb over part of it.

image.prompt: close-up of the back of a postcard covered edge to edge in tiny cramped manic handwriting, a thumb covering one corner

panels.composition: Wood reading on. Skipping. The dog's ear goes down.

balloons.text: '...guerrilla theater in a parking garage...' — skip — '...you'd hate it, you'd love hating it...' — skip —

image.prompt: a young man reading a postcard and visibly skipping lines while a dog under the table lowers its ear

panels.composition: Wood, thumb still over the last line. He doesn't read it out. He puts the card on the corkboard, thumb side to the wall.

characters.pose: pinning the card face out, back hidden

image.prompt: close-up of a hand pinning a postcard to a corkboard with its photo side facing out and its written side to the wall, no words
image.notes: The line he doesn't read stays hidden all run. The afterword can quote it or not.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: What was under his thumb: reserved.
